title_original: Hot or not? The Guardian’s film critics run the rule over the week’s UK cinema releases
excerpt_original: Brad Pitt’s grinning stuntman returns, Ariana Grande gets the lie-detector treatment, a Disney disappointment and a killer unicorn … here are all the latest film releases at a glance *** Continue reading...

blocks.text: Minotaur

blocks.alt: Scene from Minotaur: men in suits meet in a mayor’s office with a portrait of Putin behind
blocks.caption: Powerful people, gloomy with self-hate … Minotaur. Photograph: MK Productions/PA

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence The great Russian director Andrey Zvyagintsev’s first film for almost a decade is connected to the Ukraine war; it follows the ill-deeds of a mini-oligarch who comes up with a toxic new way to feed Russia’s war machine.

What our reviewer said “This is a noir thriller of infidelity and vengeful murder, lent a new meaning by the context of deadly cynicism and political bad faith, a world in which powerful people, gloomy with self-hate, have made covering up misdeeds their way of life.” Peter Bradshaw
Big Girls Don’t Cry

blocks.alt: Ani Palmer, as Sid, sits in a bathtub smoking while gazing out a window
blocks.caption: Deeply satisfying yet seemingly effortless … Ani Palmer in Big Girls Don’t Cry. Photograph: Jen Raoult

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Coming-of-age tale from writer-director Paloma Schneideman, in which a 14-year-old pretends to be someone else in a chatroom, with real-world consequences.
What our reviewer said “Schneideman’s film has a wonderfully unforced quality, unfolding in a deeply satisfying yet seemingly effortless way.” Luke Buckmaster
The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth

Summed up in a sentence David Fincher directs Quentin Tarantino’s script, which picks up from the latter’s 2019 film Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood, with Brad Pitt reprising his role as the eponymous stuntman.

What our reviewer said “It is a movie that gives us the brutality and scuzz of Ed Bunker, the urban crime-pastoral of Elmore Leonard, and naturally the classic Tarantino trope of two tough guys rolling up in a car, a little before the appointed hour, but in time for some backtalk and bickering.” Peter Bradshaw
14th

blocks.alt: Librarian of Congress Carla Hayden talks with Ava DuVernay across a desk in an office
blocks.caption: The 14th Librarian of Congress, Carla Hayden, right, with film-maker Ava DuVernay. Photograph: Paul Garnes/Netflix/AP

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Ava DuVernay’s follow-up to her dissection of the 13th amendment, which offers a vehement and exhilarating defence of democracy as she examines the issue of citizen birthright.

What our reviewer said “DuVernay sees the enemy as Maga and the constitution as something that must be defended against a tinpot bully president and his viper’s-nest court of sycophants.” Peter Bradshaw
The Slightest Touch

blocks.alt: Colin Farrell sits beside Emma Fogarty in her wheelchair, chatting at an outdoor event
blocks.caption: Big-hearted odd-couple story … Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty in The Slightest Touch. Photograph: PR

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Documentary about the friendship of Colin Farrell and Emma Fogarty, as they prepare for the Dublin marathon to raise awareness of Fogarty’s epidermolysis bullosa.
What our reviewer said “It is an unexpectedly intimate, emotional piece of work, a big-hearted odd-couple story, which is perhaps slightly more complex than at first appears.” Peter Bradshaw
The World of Love

blocks.alt: Laughing schoolgirls in uniform play around a desk in a classroom with posters
blocks.caption: School is rocked …  The World of Love. Photograph: Bulldog Film Distribution

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Compellingly elusive family mystery from South Korean director Yoon Ga-eun that tracks the uneasy fallout after a teenage schoolgirl makes a deeply shocking announcement to her class.
What our reviewer said “Yoon Ga-eun creates a strange world of bewilderment, sadness and pain – but not much of love – in this involving and mysterious family drama.” Peter Bradshaw
Who Is Still Alive

blocks.alt: A crouching man in a spotlight uses a paintbrush and bucket on the floor
blocks.caption: Grief-stricken stories … Who Is Still Alive. Photograph: Akka Films

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Nicolas Wadimoff invites Gaza refugees to draw a floor plan of their former neighbourhood, bringing to life grief-stricken stories of the places and people lost.
What our reviewer said “The raw and agonising grief, which perhaps stays just at the waterline of consciousness most of the time, is here brought above the surface.” Peter Bradshaw
Everything Else Is Noise
Summed up in a sentence Docufiction from film-maker Nicolás Pereda about a musician attempting to deal with a TV shoot in her flat.

What our reviewer said “Far from a mere backdrop, Teresa’s home gradually becomes filled with revelations of discontent, doubt and resentment. Pereda’s expert blocking, however, beautifully accentuates kinship alongside fractures.” Phuong Le
In Waves

blocks.alt: Animated still from In Waves showing two faces floating upside down in rippling water
blocks.caption: Tenderly drawn … In Waves. Photograph: Courtesy of Netflix

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Tenderly drawn story adapted from AJ Dungo’s graphic novel combines a history of surfing with an emotional account of losing a partner to bone cancer aged 24.

What our reviewer said “There is something desperately sad in the film’s nostalgic mood: Dungo still in his 20s, already looking in the rear-view at his youth like it’s a different universe.” Cath Clarke
The Boy and the Suit of Lights
Summed up in a sentence Encouraged by his grandfather and single mother, teenage Borja dreams of a career as a bullfighter that will end his family’s poverty.

What our reviewer said “Bullfighting itself is not judged; rather, she focuses on the growing controversy swirling around it, including the incensed protesters and fired-up apprentices fretting about whether anti-corrida parties will win the elections.” Phil Hoad
To Hold a Mountain

blocks.alt: Nada’s windswept hair blows across her face as Gara rides a white horse past grazing sheep
blocks.caption: Stately pastoral existence … To Hold a Mountain. Photograph: Nina Durdevic

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence A tough and savvy livestock farmer fights to stop military training taking over her breathtaking mountain home in Montenegro.

What our reviewer said “The fight against the state is just one element of a film that, through long, languid takes, reveals the women’s stately pastoral existence, one taken up above all with care for their menagerie of animals (cows, sheep, goats, cats and dogs) and each other.” Leslie Felperin
Focker-in-Law

Summed up in a sentence Skyler Gisondo and Ariana Grande join the extended Focker universe, as Greg Focker’s son and his fiancee, as the family heads to the 80th birthday celebrations of paterfamilias Jack (Robert De Niro).

What our reviewer said “The film always has a weird ingredient of bland to counteract the vinegar of comedy and the Fockers and their eternally recurring crises have become overfamiliar.” Peter Bradshaw
Hexed

blocks.alt: Animated characters Billie and Beef sit on a purple sofa, with Beef laughing in sunglasses
blocks.caption: Hollow also-ran … Hexed. Photograph: Disney Enterprises/PA

blocks.text: Summed up in a sentence Original animation from Disney in which a teen girl discovers she is witch, and heads to a magical realm with her three-eyed cat where her fellow witches are imprisoned.

What our reviewer said “There would be few greater big-screen pleasures at this moment than a true return to form for Disney, an original, invigorating crowd-pleaser to rival what so many of us grew up watching and loving, but Hexed is another hollow and glumly disappointing also-ran.” Benjamin Lee
Buddy
Summed up in a sentence Comedy horror about a murderous TV show orange unicorn dares to wonder: what if Barney killed kids?

What our reviewer said “The novelty of a malevolent presence in the wholesome, brightly lit world of a kids TV show can’t quite sustain an engaging 95-minute feature, writer-director Casper Kelly not knowing where to take his admittedly attention-securing setup.” Benjamin Lee
